recipes.name: Nopal Katsu Sando
ingredients: Optional: thin layer of butter, pickled red onion, or hot sauce
instructions: Generously salt the trimmed Nopal paddle and let them cure for 1-12 hours, depending on your slime preference. - 3 trimmed Nopal (cactus) paddles - kosher salt to taste
Rinse thoroughly and pat dry. - 3 trimmed Nopal (cactus) paddles
In a small saucepan, heat oil and lightly fry garlic until golden. - ½ cup neutral oil - 4 cloves garlic

Add dried chilies, peanuts, and sesame seeds, and cook until fragrant. Don’t let the chilies burn! - 6 chiles de árbol - 2 dried Guajillo chiles - 2 dried Pasilla chiles - ¼ cup peanuts - 2 tbsp sesame seeds
Transfer to a blender or food processor blend into a thick, chunky chili crisp. - For the Salsa Macha Mayo
Combine half of the mixture with mayo, and save the rest for later. - ½ cup mayonnaise
Mix purple cabbage with lime juice, chopped cilantro, and a pinch of salt. - 1 cup shredded purple cabbage - 2 tbsp lime juice - 2 tbsp chopped cilantro - pinch of salt

Set up your breading station in 3 separate wide, shallow bowls, one bowl with all-purpose flour, one bowl with 2 beaten eggs, a pinch of salt and a splash of water, and the last bowl with Panko breadcrumbs. - 1 cup all purpose flour - 2 eggs beaten - pinch of salt - 1 ½ cups Panko breadcrumbs

Dredge the cured Nopal paddles in flour then dip in the beaten egg, and generously coat in panko. - 3 trimmed Nopal (cactus) paddles - 1 cup all purpose flour - 2 eggs beaten - 1 ½ cups Panko breadcrumbs
Shallow fry in neutral oil at 350°F, about 2-3 minutes per side. - neutral oil for frying
Drain on a wire cooling rack set over a rimmed baking sheet. - For the Nopal Katsu

Toast the milk bread, then slather each side with the Salsa Macha Mayo, add a bed of Slaw, and finally top with the crispy Nopal cutlet. Crown with a final slice of toasted milk bread. - soft milk bread or Shokupan - For the Salsa Macha Mayo - For the Slaw - For the Nopal Katsu
